title: Hiroki Yoshida （吉田 拓暉）
text:
I study quantum-geometric and symmetry-protected phenomena in topological and altermagnetic systems. My research focuses on nonlinear transport, Berry-phase effects, and quantization mechanisms in Weyl semimetals, using tight-binding modeling and symmetry-based analysis.
Research interests: quantum geometry · nonlinear transport · topological phases · altermagnetism · magnetoelastic phenomena

title: Research
text: My research is in theoretical condensed matter physics, with an emphasis on quantum geometry, topology, symmetry, and nonlinear response phenomena. I mainly use tight-binding models and symmetry-based analysis to identify robust transport and optical effects.

title: Research
text:
Quantum geometry and nonlinear responses
I study how geometric properties of Bloch states appear in measurable nonlinear responses. This includes the divergence of shift-current responses near a two-dimensional Weyl-semimetal limit [1], the emergent-gravity Hall effect associated with quantum geometry [2], and light-induced magnetization generated by quantum-geometric effects [3].

title: Research
text:
Altermagnets and spin photovoltaic effects
A major recent direction is nonlinear spin transport in altermagnetic systems. In particular, I developed a theoretical framework for a quantized spin-current analogue of the circular photogalvanic effect in altermagnetic Weyl semimetals, combining symmetry classification with tight-binding modeling [4].

title: Research
text:
Two-dimensional Weyl semimetal limits
I have studied discontinuous changes of electric polarization around topological phase transitions in two-dimensional systems, including symmetry breaking in two-dimensional Weyl semimetals [5] and polarization jumps across topological phase transitions [6].

title: Research
text:
Magnetoelastic waves
I also work on coupled magnetic and elastic excitations in ferromagnetic thin films, including magnetoelastic waves mediated by dipolar interactions [7].
